step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core components from visual inventory and audio transcript: CloudWatch event trigger, Monitoring Lambda, DynamoDB database, Allocation/De-allocation Lambda, and EC2 application instances representing the hot encoder pool.
2. Validated all service names against the strict AWS vocabulary list: CloudWatch, Lambda, DynamoDB, EC2.
3. Defined Flow 0 for scheduled capacity monitoring: CloudWatch fires every minute, triggering Monitoring Lambda, which calls Allocation/De-allocation Lambda if adjustments are necessary.
4. Defined Flow 1 for dynamic user-driven allocation: User activity writes to DynamoDB, streaming updates to Allocation/De-allocation Lambda, which provisions/ configures the EC2 hot pool instances.

graph.name: Grabyo Serverless Hot Pool Orchestration and Video Encoding Architecture
graph.notes: Grabyo uses a serverless orchestration layer featuring CloudWatch, Lambda, and DynamoDB Streams to manage a hot pool of EC2 instances running custom video processing and encoding logic.

nodes.name: CloudWatch
nodes.notes: Fires scheduled events every 1 minute to initiate health and capacity monitoring.

nodes.name: Monitoring Lambda
nodes.notes: Checks instance health and evaluates capacity requirements (over/under provisioning).

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores UI interaction states and triggers downstream allocation via DynamoDB Streams.

nodes.name: Allocation/De-allocation Lambda
nodes.notes: Orchestrates EC2 hot spare assignment and EC2 provisioning/de-allocation requests.

nodes.name: EC2 (Upper)
nodes.notes: Compute instance running custom video processing logic for live streams.

nodes.name: EC2 (Lower)
nodes.notes: Compute instance running custom video processing logic for live streams.

edges.notes: CloudWatch triggers Monitoring Lambda every minute.
Monitoring Lambda invokes Allocation/De-allocation Lambda if scaling adjustments are required.
DynamoDB Streams triggers Allocation/De-allocation Lambda upon object updates from user interactions.
Allocation/De-allocation Lambda configures or provisions upper EC2 instance.
Allocation/De-allocation Lambda configures or provisions lower EC2 instance.
